chunks: Therefore, man should secure honour by adopting these qualities. He should fear the day of Doom before it arrives, and he should appreciate the shortness of his life and the shortness of his sojourn in the place of stay which has only to last for his change over to the next place. He should therefore do something for his change over and for the known stages of his departure.

key_terms.قَارِعَةً: A striking calamity or event (often referring to Death or the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.مَعَارِفِ مُنْتَقَلِهِ: The known stages of his departure/destination
key_terms.مَنْزِلٍ: Dwelling or abode (referring to the world)

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about preparing for death and the afterlife?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of a transient dwelling to emphasize the impermanence of worldly life, urging believers to actively prepare their spiritual provisions for the eternal abode. This exhortation reflects the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a conscious readiness for death through righteous deeds, ensuring a smooth transition from the temporary world to the permanent hereafter.
